newsitem.title: BELARUS: Three Belarus constitutional court judges resign.
newsitem.headline: Three Belarus constitutional court judges resign.

text.p: Three judges of Belarus's 11-member Constitutional court, including its head, resigned on Tuesday in protest at President Alexander Lukashenko's policies.

The court's chairman Valery Tikhinya, Alexander Vashkevich and Mikhail Pastukhov decided they could not serve under Lukashenko's constitution which gave him sweeping powers and was passed by referendum last month, Pastukhov told Reuters by telephone.
"The law was broken many times during the plebiscite. We do not recognise the constitution. We do not believe in it, we do not consider it legitimate and we cannot serve under it," Pastukhov said.

The judges handed their resignations to Semyon Sharetsky, the head of the parliament dissolved by a new house assembled by Lukashenko after he won an overwhelming mandate to rewrite the constitution, Pastukhov said.

The referendum and constitution have been widely criticised and Europe's biggest security body, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said on Tuesday that voting "was conducted in contradiction with constitutional procedures and cannot be considered as legitimate".
The president, attending an OSCE summit in the Portuguese capital, shrugged off its criticism and told it not to meddle.
